Fully Funded Position at The University of Glasgow, Animal-Computer Interaction Lab, United Kingdom

I am recruiting for a fully funded PhD position as part of FUTUREFAUNA, my ERC Starting Grant project, which I lead at the University of Glasgow.

The PhD will investigate how animals can use computing technology to gain greater control over their environment and choice over their social connections. The overarching goal is to build a comprehensive, empirically grounded framework for designing, implementing, and adapting technology for animal users.

Start date: 1st October 2026 (but can be sooner)

Funding: Fully funded (fees + UKRI stipend rate) for UK and EU citizens

The recruited PhD student will focus on designing and building bespoke interactive interfaces centred around animal needs, with a focus on pets or zoo animals. You will develop technology for and with animals, with opportunities to deepen technical skills in interactive systems (hardware and/or software).

I welcome applicants with backgrounds in HCI, interaction design, or related fields. Experience with qualitative and/or quantitative research methods and user studies is desirable. Prior experience with animals is beneficial but not required.

The successful candidate will join the interdisciplinary Animal-Computer Interaction Group (

). We are a small, growing group that includes PhDs and Postdocs, and we regularly publish at ACM CHI (where you can find us next month, presenting our papers!).
